sn22.85:1.1: On one occasion the Venerable Sāriputta was dwelling at Savatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anathapiṇḍika’s Park.
sn22.85:1.2: Now on that occasion the following pernicious view had arisen in a bhikkhu named Yamaka:
sn22.85:1.3: “As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed is annihilated and perishes with the breakup of the body and does not exist after death.”
sn22.85:2.1: A number of bhikkhus heard that such a pernicious view had arisen in the bhikkhu Yamaka.
sn22.85:2.3: Then they approached the Venerable Yamaka and exchanged greetings with him,
sn22.85:2.4: after which they sat down to one side and said to him:
sn22.85:3.1: “Is it true, friend Yamaka, that such a pernicious view as this has arisen in you:
sn22.85:3.2: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed is annihilated and perishes with the breakup of the body and does not exist after death’?”
sn22.85:3.3: “Exactly so, friends. As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed is annihilated and perishes with the breakup of the body and does not exist after death.”
sn22.85:4.1: “Friend Yamaka, do not speak thus. Do not misrepresent the Blessed One. It is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One. The Blessed One would not speak thus:
sn22.85:4.2: ‘A bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed is annihilated and perishes with the breakup of the body and does not exist after death.’”
sn22.85:4.3: Yet, although he was admonished by the bhikkhus in this way, the Venerable Yamaka still obstinately grasped that pernicious view, adhered to it, and declared:
sn22.85:4.4: “As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed is annihilated and perishes with the breakup of the body and does not exist after death.”
sn22.85:5.1: Since those bhikkhus were unable to detach the Venerable Yamaka from that pernicious view, they rose from their seats, approached the Venerable Sāriputta, and told him all that had occurred, adding:
sn22.85:5.4: “It would be good if the Venerable Sāriputta would approach the bhikkhu Yamaka out of compassion for him.”
sn22.85:5.5: The Venerable Sāriputta consented by silence.
sn22.85:5.6: Then, in the evening, the Venerable Sāriputta emerged from seclusion. He approached the Venerable Yamaka and exchanged greetings with him, after which he sat down to one side and said to him:
sn22.85:6.1: “Is it true, friend Yamaka, that such a pernicious view as this has arisen in you:
sn22.85:6.2: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed is annihilated and perishes with the breakup of the body and does not exist after death’?”

sn22.85:12.1: “Formerly, friend Sāriputta, when I was ignorant, I did hold that pernicious view,
sn22.85:12.2: but now that I have heard this Dhamma teaching of the Venerable Sāriputta I have abandoned that pernicious view and have made the breakthrough to the Dhamma.”

sn22.85:28.7: “So it is, friend Sāriputta, for those venerable ones who have such compassionate and benevolent brothers in the holy life to admonish and instruct them.
sn22.85:28.8: And now that I have heard this Dhamma teaching of the Venerable Sāriputta, my mind is liberated from the taints by nonclinging.” This is what the Venerable Sāriputta said. Elated, the Venerable Yamaka delighted in the Venerable Sāriputta’s statement.
